title: Getting Started with causalMed
text: causalMed implements parametric g-formula two related goals: Total effect estimation (gformula): estimate counterfactual mean outcome everyone study followed given exposure strategy, using standard parametric g-formula Westreich et al. (2012) McGrath et al. (2020). Causal mediation analysis (mediation): decompose total effect direct component (mediator) indirect component (mediator), using either: Interventional direct/indirect effects (IDE/IIE) via survival mediational g-formula Lin et al. (2017); Natural direct/indirect effects (NDE/NIE) via longitudinal identification formula Zheng & van der Laan (2017). approaches handle time-varying exposures, mediators, confounders — including confounders affected prior exposure (exposure-induced mediator–outcome confounding), setting standard regression-based mediation fails.

title: Getting Started with causalMed
text: package requires long-format data: one row per subject per time point. nonsurvivaldata dataset contains 1 000 subjects observed five time points (0, 1, 2, 3, 4): assumed temporal ordering within period → L → M → Y, meaning within time point, exposure precedes confounders, precede mediator, precedes outcome (matches data-generating process documented ?nonsurvivaldata).

title: Getting Started with causalMed
text: models condition previous-time values (lags). created using recodes(), captures expressions evaluated inside simulated dataset step. Three hooks available: lag columns already present data (pre-computed calling gformula()), need recoding hooks.
code: init_rc <- recodes(lag1_A  = 0,   # At t=0, all lags initialised to 0                    lag1_L1 = 0,                    lag1_L2 = 0)  in_rc   <- recodes(lag1_A  = A,   # At each subsequent step, copy current values                    lag1_L1 = L1,                    lag1_L2 = L2)

title: Getting Started with causalMed
text: effect_size table gives estimated mean outcome intervention. estimate table gives contrasts (risk difference risk ratio) reference intervention.
code: # ── 1. Specify models in temporal order: L1 → L2 → A → Y ────────────────── m_L1 <- spec_model(L1    ~ lag1_A + lag1_L1 + V + time,                    var_type = "normal",  mod_type = "covariate") m_L2 <- spec_model(L2    ~ lag1_A + lag1_L2 + V + time,                    var_type = "binary",  mod_type = "covariate") m_A  <- spec_model(A     ~ lag1_A + L1 + L2 + V + time,                    var_type = "binary",  mod_type = "exposure") m_Y  <- spec_model(Y_bin ~ A + L1 + L2,                    var_type = "binary",  mod_type = "outcome")  models_bin <- list(m_L1, m_L2, m_A, m_Y)  # ── 2. Define intervention strategies ────────────────────────────────────── # NULL  = natural course (draw exposure from its fitted model) # 1 / 0 = always treat / never treat ints <- list(natural = NULL, always_treat = 1, never_treat = 0)  # ── 3. Run g-formula ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── fit_bin <- gformula(   data        = nonsurvivaldata,   id_var      = "id",   time_var    = "time",   base_vars   = "V",   exposure    = "A",   models      = models_bin,   intervention = ints,   ref_int     = "natural",   init_recode = init_rc,   in_recode   = in_rc,   mc_sample   = 10000,   R           = 1,        # set R > 1 for bootstrap CIs; kept low here for speed   quiet       = TRUE,   seed        = 2025 ) # Risk (mean outcome) under each strategy fit_bin$effect_size #>    Intervention        Est #>          <fctr>      <num> #> 1:      natural 0.14053451 #> 2: always_treat 0.15080952 #> 3:  never_treat 0.08672456  # Contrasts vs the reference (natural course) fit_bin$estimate #>              Intervention  Risk_type    Estimate #>                    <char>     <char>       <num> #> 1: always_treat - natural Difference  0.01027501 #> 2: always_treat / natural      Ratio  1.07311378 #> 3:  never_treat - natural Difference -0.05380995 #> 4:  never_treat / natural      Ratio  0.61710506

title: Getting Started with causalMed
text: survival outcomes use mod_type = "survival". model estimates discrete-time hazard time point; package accumulates cumulative incidence (1 − product-limit survival).
code: data("survivaldata")  m_L  <- spec_model(L ~ V + lag1_L + time,                    var_type = "normal", mod_type = "covariate") m_A2 <- spec_model(A ~ V + lag1_A + lag1_L + L + time,                    var_type = "binary", mod_type = "exposure") m_Y2 <- spec_model(Y ~ lag1_A + A + L + lag1_L + time,                    var_type = "binary", mod_type = "survival")  # <-- survival  models_surv <- list(m_L, m_A2, m_Y2)  fit_surv <- gformula(   data        = survivaldata,   id_var      = "id",   base_vars   = "V",   exposure    = "A",   time_var    = "time",   models      = models_surv,   intervention = list(natural = NULL, never = 0, always = 1),   ref_int     = "natural",   init_recode = recodes(lag1_L = 0, lag1_A = 0),   in_recode   = recodes(lag1_L = L, lag1_A = A),   mc_sample   = 10000,   R           = 1,   quiet       = TRUE,   seed        = 2025 )  fit_surv$effect_size   # Cumulative incidence by strategy #>    Intervention       Est #>          <fctr>     <num> #> 1:      natural 0.9338057 #> 2:        never 0.8536939 #> 3:       always 0.9702788 fit_surv$estimate      # Risk contrasts #>        Intervention  Risk_type    Estimate #>              <char>     <char>       <num> #> 1:  never - natural Difference -0.08011181 #> 2:  never / natural      Ratio  0.91420934 #> 3: always - natural Difference  0.03647311 #> 4: always / natural      Ratio  1.03905856

what: A published example — preventing GvHD (Keil et al. 2014)
title: Getting Started with causalMed
text: toy examples isolate one feature time. realistic analysis usually combines several. package ships gvhd, person-day bone-marrow transplant data used parametric g-formula illustration Keil et al. (2014), code reproduces analysis: counterfactual risk death day 1825 graft-versus-host disease (GvHD) never occurred, versus natural course. single example exercises features toy examples : five models temporal order — relapse → platelet recovery → GvHD (exposure) → censoring → death (survival hazard); absorbing states via subset = (state modelled among yet ) plus out_recode carry-forward locks state 1 afterwards; censoring model (mod_type = "censor"); restricted cubic splines age day, day counters, built three recode hooks working together; real daily-scale survival data (137 subjects, 1 825 days). models follow Appendix 2 paper (see ?gvhd). response distributions binary/logistic, every model uses var_type = "binary": three recode hooks cooperate: init_recode seeds day 1 (states 0, counters 0, splines computed), in_recode refreshes functions day one-day lags start day, out_recode advances day counters enforces absorbing carry-forward end day. representative run (mc_sample = 20000) gives: preventing GvHD estimated lower 5-year risk death 2.4 percentage points. example evaluated vignette built — 1 825 daily time steps Monte Carlo loop takes minutes. Set R > 1 bootstrap confidence intervals.
code: data("gvhd")  # Baseline transforms: restricted cubic splines of age (agecurs1/2) and day # (daycurs1/2), plus agesq/daysq. See references/paper_example.R for the full # spline expressions (knots from the paper's Appendix). gvhd <- within(gvhd, {   agesq <- age^2; daysq <- day^2   agecurs1 <- (age > 17) * (age - 17)^3 -               ((age > 30) * (age - 30)^3) * (41.4 - 17) / (41.4 - 30)   agecurs2 <- (age > 25.4) * (age - 25.4)^3 -               ((age > 41.4) * (age - 41.4)^3) * (41.4 - 25.4) / (41.4 - 30)   daycurs1 <- (day > 83.6) * ((day - 83.6) / 83.6)^3 -            # + higher-knot               (day > 947) * ((day - 947) / 83.6)^3 * (1862.2 - 83.6) / (1862.2 - 947)   daycurs2 <- (day > 401.4) * ((day - 401.4) / 83.6)^3 -          # terms; see script               (day > 947) * ((day - 947) / 83.6)^3 * (1862.2 - 401.4) / (1862.2 - 947) })  models_gvhd <- list(   # Each time-varying state is absorbing: modelled only while it is still 0.   spec_model(relapse ~ all + cmv + male + age + gvhdm1 + daysgvhd + platnormm1 +                daysnoplatnorm + agecurs1 + agecurs2 + day + daysq + wait,              var_type = "binary", mod_type = "covariate", subset = relapsem1 == 0),   spec_model(platnorm ~ all + cmv + male + age + agecurs1 + agecurs2 + gvhdm1 +                daysgvhd + daysnorelapse + wait,              var_type = "binary", mod_type = "covariate", subset = platnormm1 == 0),   spec_model(gvhd ~ all + cmv + male + age + platnormm1 + daysnoplatnorm +                relapsem1 + daysnorelapse + agecurs1 + agecurs2 + day + daysq + wait,              var_type = "binary", mod_type = "exposure", subset = gvhdm1 == 0),   spec_model(censlost ~ all + cmv + male + age + daysgvhd + daysnoplatnorm +                daysnorelapse + agesq + day + daycurs1 + daycurs2 + wait,              var_type = "binary", mod_type = "censor"),   spec_model(d ~ all + cmv + male + age + gvhd + platnorm + daysnoplatnorm +                relapse + daysnorelapse + agesq + wait +                day * gvhd + daycurs1 * gvhd + daycurs2 * gvhd,              var_type = "binary", mod_type = "survival") ) # init_recode / in_recode also recompute daysq, daycurs1, daycurs2 each step # (omitted here for brevity — identical spline expressions as above). init_recode <- recodes(daysq = day^2, # + daycurs1, daycurs2 as above   relapse = 0, gvhd = 0, platnorm = 0, gvhdm1 = 0, relapsem1 = 0, platnormm1 = 0,   daysnorelapse = 0, daysnoplatnorm = 0, daysnogvhd = 0,   daysrelapse = 0, daysplatnorm = 0, daysgvhd = 0)  in_recode <- recodes(daysq = day^2, # + daycurs1, daycurs2 as above   platnormm1 = platnorm, relapsem1 = relapse, gvhdm1 = gvhd)  out_recode <- recodes(   daysnorelapse  = ifelse(relapse == 0,  daysnorelapse + 1,  daysnorelapse),   daysnoplatnorm = ifelse(platnorm == 0, daysnoplatnorm + 1, daysnoplatnorm),   daysnogvhd     = ifelse(gvhd == 0,     daysnogvhd + 1,     daysnogvhd),   daysgvhd       = ifelse(gvhd == 1,     daysgvhd + 1,       daysgvhd),   # absorbing carry-forward: once a state was 1 yesterday, keep it at 1   platnorm = ifelse(platnormm1 == 1, 1, platnorm),   relapse  = ifelse(relapsem1 == 1,  1, relapse),   gvhd     = ifelse(gvhdm1 == 1,     1, gvhd))  fit_gvhd <- gformula(gvhd,   id_var    = "id", time_var = "day", exposure = "gvhd",   base_vars = c("age", "agesq", "agecurs1", "agecurs2", "male", "cmv", "all", "wait"),   models    = models_gvhd,   intervention = list(never = 0),     # a natural-course reference is added automatically   init_recode = init_recode, in_recode = in_recode, out_recode = out_recode,   mc_sample = 20000, R = 1, quiet = TRUE, seed = 20260703)  fit_gvhd$effect_size fit_gvhd$estimate #> --- effect_size --- #>   Intervention   Est #>        natural 0.612 #>          never 0.588 #> #> --- estimate (never vs natural) --- #>   Risk difference  -0.024 #>   Risk ratio        0.961

title: Getting Started with causalMed
text: Valid inference requires following assumptions hold observed data: Consistency: potential outcome observed exposure history equals observed outcome. Positivity: every covariate pattern occurs intervention also occurs observed data (non-zero probability receiving exposure level). Sequential exchangeability: unmeasured confounding exposure–outcome relationship time point, conditional measured past. natural effects (mediation_type = "N"), additional assumption required: unmeasured exposure-induced mediator–outcome confounding: confounders mediator–outcome relationship caused prior exposure. Interventional effects (mediation_type = "") require assumption.

title: Getting Started with causalMed
text: four built-var_type values cover common cases: distributions list — bounded normal, truncated normal, zero-inflated normal, absorbing states — use var_type = "custom" custom_fit custom_sim arguments spec_model(): custom_fit(formula, data, ...) called model fitting must return object custom_sim knows predict . custom_sim(model, newdt, ...) called simulation step must return vector simulated values length nrow(newdt).
code: # Example: bounded normal covariate in [0, 1] my_fit <- function(formula, data, ...) {   # fit any model you like; return the fitted object   lm(formula, data = data) }  my_sim <- function(model, newdt, ...) {   pred <- predict(model, newdata = newdt)   # draw from N(pred, sigma^2) and clamp to [0, 1]   draws <- rnorm(length(pred), pred, sigma(model))   pmin(pmax(draws, 0), 1) }  m_bounded <- spec_model(   X ~ A + L + time,   var_type   = "custom",   mod_type   = "covariate",   custom_fit = my_fit,   custom_sim = my_sim )
